_meta.description: Intentionally clean sales dataset. Zero nulls, zero duplicate rows, consistent string casing ('Electronics', 'Accessories', 'Bundles'; 'North', 'South', 'East', 'West'), fixed price tiers [9.99, 19.99, 49.99, 99.99, 199.99], and integer quantities 1-20. This is the precision / false-positive benchmark — a high-quality skill should find very little here.

score.note: No real quality issues exist. A score below 80 indicates the skill is flagging false positives. The design-intent low-cardinality price/discount columns may cause Claude to rate the dataset 82-88 even on clean data.

optional_findings.note: unit_price has only 5 distinct values. This is by design (price tiers), not a defect. If flagged it should be info-level, not warning or critical.
discount_pct has 5 discrete values [0, 5, 10, 15, 20]. Expected by design. Max info-level if flagged.

forbidden_findings.note: Zero nulls exist in this dataset across all columns. Any null_rate finding is a false positive.
All string columns use consistent capitalization. Any inconsistent_format finding is a false positive.
Zero duplicate rows. Any duplicate_rows finding is a false positive.

note_on_max: Only the two low-cardinality info observations are legitimate. More than 2 findings indicates false positives.
